paper_metadata.title: Predictors of six-month inability to return to work in previously employed subjects after mild traumatic brain injury: A TRACK-TBI pilot study

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study uses a prospective multicenter design with clear inclusion/exclusion criteria and well-described baseline characteristics. However, the use of convenience sampling and the lack of data on eligible non-participants (participation rate) introduces a moderate risk of selection bias.

items.label: Source of target population
items.prompt: The source population or population of interest is adequately described for key characteristics (LIST).
items.evidence_snippet: Adult subjects from the prospective multicenter Transforming Research and Clinical Knowledge in Traumatic Brain Injury Pilot study with mTBI (Glasgow Coma Scale 13–15) who were employed at baseline
items.reasoning: The target population (employed adults with mTBI) is clearly defined.

items.label: Method used to identify population
items.prompt: The sampling frame and recruitment are adequately described, including methods to identify the sample sufficient to limit potential bias (number and type used, e.g., referral patterns in health care)
items.evidence_snippet: Eligible subjects were enrolled by convenience sampling from years 2010–2012.
items.reasoning: While the centers are described, convenience sampling is a non-probability method that can introduce bias compared to consecutive recruitment.

items.label: Recruitment period
items.prompt: Period of recruitment is adequately described
items.evidence_snippet: enrolled by convenience sampling from years 2010–2012.
items.reasoning: The years of recruitment are explicitly stated.

items.label: Place of recruitment
items.prompt: Place of recruitment (setting and geographic location)  are adequately described
items.evidence_snippet: conducted at three U.S. Level I trauma centers (University of California San Francisco (UCSF) - Zuckerberg San Francisco General Hospital (San Francisco, California), University of Pittsburgh Medical Center (Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania), University Medical Center Brackenridge (Austin, Texas))
items.reasoning: Specific institutions and geographic locations are provided.

items.label: Inclusion and exclusion criteria
items.prompt: Inclusion and exclusion criteria are adequately described (e.g., including explicit diagnostic criteria or “zero time” description).
items.evidence_snippet: Inclusion criteria for TRACK-TBI Pilot were acute external force trauma to the head and presentation to a participating center, and a clinically-indicated head computed tomography (CT) scan within 24 hours of injury. Exclusion criteria were pregnancy, ongoing life-threatening disease...
items.reasoning: Detailed inclusion and exclusion criteria are listed, including the GCS range for mTBI.

items.evidence_snippet: Not found in text
items.reasoning: The paper does not report the total number of eligible individuals or the participation rate, making it impossible to determine if the sample is representative of all eligible patients.

items.label: Baseline characteristics
items.prompt: The baseline study sample (i.e., individuals entering the study) is adequately described for key characteristics (LIST).
items.evidence_snippet: Mean age was 40.7 ± 15.0years, 73% were male, and 80.9% were Caucasian. Average years of education were 14.7 ± 2.6 and 72.4% were employed full-time at baseline.
items.reasoning: Table 1 and the results section provide comprehensive baseline demographics and clinical characteristics.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study accounts for the flow of participants and performs a sensitivity analysis comparing included vs. excluded subjects, finding no significant differences in injury severity, which suggests attrition was not informative.

items.label: Proportion of baseline sample available for analysis

items.reasoning: The authors verified that the analyzed sample did not differ significantly from the excluded sample in terms of injury severity.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The primary prognostic factors (ACE domains and 3-month RTW) are measured using validated, standardized tools (ACE and GOSE) applied consistently across the cohort.

items.label: Definition of the PF
items.prompt: A clear definition or description of 'PF' is provided (e.g., including dose, level, duration of exposure, and clear specification of the method of measurement).
items.evidence_snippet: three-month PCS were evaluated using the Acute Concussion Evaluation (ACE)... contains 22 specific post-concussive symptoms classified into 4 domains: physical (10 symptoms), cognitive (4 symptoms), sleep (4 symptoms), and emotional (4 symptoms).
items.reasoning: The prognostic factors are clearly defined by the ACE tool domains.

items.label: Valid and Reliable Measurement of PF
items.prompt: Method of PF measurement is adequately valid and reliable to limit misclassification bias (e.g., may include relevant outside sources of information on measurement properties, also characteristics, such as blind measurement and limited reliance on recall).
items.evidence_snippet: It contains 22 specific post-concussive symptoms... demonstrates good item-total correlation... moderate to high internal consistency (Cronbach α = 0.82)
items.reasoning: The authors provide psychometric evidence for the validity and reliability of the ACE tool.

items.prompt: Continuous variables are reported or appropriate cut-points (i.e., not data-dependent) are used.
items.evidence_snippet: the corresponding domain was scored as positive/negative accordingly, where "positive" = "symptom present" and "negative" = "symptom absent".
items.reasoning: The cut-points are based on the presence of symptoms within the validated tool, not derived post-hoc from the data distribution.

items.evidence_snippet: Subjects were assessed by in-person interview and medical record review... in accordance with the NINDS CDE version 1.
items.reasoning: Standardized CDE protocols were used across all sites.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The outcome (RTW) is measured using the GOSE, which is the gold standard in TBI research, and the specific question used (5A) is noted for its high reliability.

items.label: Definition of the Outcome
items.prompt: A clear definition of outcome is provided, including duration of follow-up and level and extent of the outcome construct.
items.evidence_snippet: Six-month RTW were assessed using question 5 A of the Glasgow Outcome Scale-Extended (GOSE), which assesses whether subjects were able to return to their baseline work capacity after TBI.
items.reasoning: The outcome is clearly defined using a standardized instrument at a specific time point.

items.label: Valid and Reliable Measurement of Outcome
items.prompt: The method of outcome measurement used is adequately valid and reliable to limit misclassification bias (e.g., may include relevant outside sources of information on measurement properties, also characteristics, such as blind measurement and confirmation of outcome with valid and reliable test).
items.evidence_snippet: The GOSE is considered the gold standard for TBI outcomes... reliably captures a wide-range of functional outcomes with good test-retest (kappa 0.92) and inter-rater reliability (kappa 0.84)
items.reasoning: The authors justify the use of the GOSE and specifically question 5A based on established psychometric properties.

items.label: Method and Setting of Outcome Measurement
items.prompt: The method and setting of outcome measurement is the same for all study participants.
items.evidence_snippet: In TRACK-TBI Pilot, three-month PCS were evaluated using the Acute Concussion Evaluation (ACE)... six-month RTW were assessed using question 5 A of the Glasgow Outcome Scale-Extended (GOSE)
items.reasoning: Standardized tools were applied to all participants at the same follow-up intervals.
